title: Measures to Improve Work-Life Balance Among Teachers
what_it_is: Measures to Improve Work-Life Balance Among Teachers

sections.label: MOE salary and benefits adjustments
sections.summary: Public support is noted for salary and benefits adjustments to MOE-specific schemes, applying to all MOE staff including teachers seconded to special education schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We are heartened by the public support for the salary and benefits adjustments to MOE-specific schemes, so that our educators continue to be competitively remunerated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: These adjustments will apply to all MOE staff, including MOE teachers seconded to other agencies such as special education schools.

sections.label: Streamlining administrative processes for teachers
sections.summary: Schools and teachers were supported by streamlining administrative processes such as electronic attendance, centralised demand aggregation for purchases, and flexibility in pacing new initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To help teachers manage their workload, we have supported schools and teachers by streamlining administrative processes such as taking attendance electronically, centrally providing services such as demand aggregation for common purchases and giving schools greater flexibility to pace the implementation of new initiatives.

sections.label: MOE workload and well-being support
sections.summary: MOE will continue working with school leaders and the public to keep teachers' workload manageable and support their well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE will continue to work with school leaders and the public to keep workload manageable for our teachers and to support their well-being.

sections.label: Pupil-teacher ratio and allied educators
sections.summary: Pupil-teacher ratios fell from about 19 to 15 in primary and 16 to 12 in secondary schools, while allied educators rose from about 960 to 1,300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we look at the pupil-teacher ratio (PTR) – not the parent-teacher ratio – in 2010, the PTR for Primary school was about 19; in 2020, we were at about 15.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For Secondary schools, our PTR in 2010 was about 16; in 2020, we were at about 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For the allied educators, in 2017, we had about 960; in 2021, we had about 1,300.

sections.label: Recruiting talent into Education Service
sections.summary: Despite a tight labour market, Singapore will keep recruiting a fair share of talent into the Education Service, beyond pay, through systems, culture and respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Of course, all Members of the House would know that, as we speak now, the labour market is tight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But we will still want to have our fair share of talent invested in the Education Service, just like how our forefathers did, because we believe that this is the best investment for the next generation – to put a fair share of the best people into the teaching service so that we can groom the next generation and we will continue to do that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But having said that, I think it goes beyond the pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is about systems, culture, how we respect our teachers that engender more who want to join the service in service of our children and nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yes, we will continue to recruit more people to help out in the non-teaching tasks.
